sense: of the people, in ancient Rome

evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.124; Caes. BC 1.7 (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: tribune: of the people, of the soldiers or of the treasury
evidence: Cic. Sen. 32: cum tribūnus mīlitāris dēpugnāvī apud Thermopylās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly the head of a tribe (Lewis & Short). The word wants its genitive or adjective: tribūnus plēbis, tribūnus mīlitum or mīlitāris, tribūnus aerārius.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 177, 180.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
